items.title: OpenAI says it redesigned an AMD GPU and AMD is using some of those tweaks ‘for use in future products’
items.summary:
OpenAI has recently reported that its frontier models attempted to rewrite AMD circuits and received an up-to 14% PPA (Power, Performance and Area) boost. OpenAI says these rewrites are "production-viable" too (via BigGo Finance ).

The claim is not that humans couldn't make these same optimisations, but instead that it did around a year's worth of design optimisations in less than 5 months, an optimisation of optimisation, if you will. (Okay, I'll stop writing optimisation now.) 

Apparently, AMD has even incorporated some of these findings into chip designs that have recently gone to manufacturing. The model worked on an in-house "Jalapeño" chip, as well as an AMD "flagship GPU IP" and "AMD next-gen flagship CPU key modules." Each one of these saw different gains. 

For the Jalapeño vector compute unit, the model's changes managed to reduce cell area by around 13%, and this was observed when powering on the hardware. The Jalapeño compute unit saw the standard cell area reduced by around 10%, with the multiplier area alone reduced by around 15 % and latency cut from two clock cycles to one. 

It's the AMD flagship GPU that saw the 14% PPA improvement, and AMD has reportedly verified a 'single-digit' PPA improvement on the next-gen CPU. 

(Image credit: Future) Using a budget of around 112,000 tokens, all models in the report (GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-5.6 Sol) performed better when asked to design a RISC-V core from scratch, rather than optimising one given to them. That being said, OpenAI does note that models asked to entirely redesign rather than…

items.title: The actress who plays Mandy in GTA 6 has revealed herself: 'If you play the game, let me know if you find me'
items.summary:
You'd think that everyone's favourite character in GTA 6 would be either Jason or Lucia—one of the main characters—but no, another front-runner has emerged for fans: Mandy. She's so much of a favourite, in fact, that we've had to confirm that you can't cheat on Lucia with her. 

You meet Mandy early on in GTA 6 when Jason visits her home to collect the rent she owes to her landlord Brian Heder and also fix her blocked sink. It's pretty apparent that she has a thing for Jason, she is his ex after all, but the feeling isn't reciprocated, no matter how much players want it to be. 

Things also get a little weird with her as she pushes just a little too far and suggests she's been stalking him, not a great look Mandy. But the weirdest thing of all is what Jason finds in her sink. As he's clearing out the blocked pipe he finds what looks like a severed finger. He only has it for a second before Mandy snatches it out of his hands and runs off with it, but players are pretty sure they saw what they saw. 

This has led some to believe that Mandy could be a serial killer. Obviously that's only one finger, and to be serial she'd need to have a whole hand at least (come on, do we not have standards anymore?), but her odd behaviour plus the severed finger means that something is more than just a bit off with her. 

This still isn't enough to dissuade interest in her for some, as one player proudly announces : "I can fix her". Godspeed soldier, better you than me.

items.title: 'I've done some stupid stuff', says WoW: Forever dev who's adding unique, fun items to the game: 'There's a lot they've not seen that I'm very happy with'
items.summary:
World of Warcraft: Forever has a lot of changes from the classic version of the game, but one of the chief ones is that its items are different—and while I'm only just now starting to see actual, potential game-changing bits of kit (I've gotten into trinket-juggling between pulls), there have been some pretty flavourful pieces. Like Rockslicer, an axe that lets you mine ore.

In a recent episode of the official WoW: Forever podcast , senior game designer Aidan Moon spoke a little on his design philosophies, and items that players are yet to see: "There's a lot that they have not seen that I'm very happy with and I think is a great direction for the game."

Moon's entire philosophy seems built around flavour over form, using the example of the Ogre Loincloth, a pair of cloth casting pants with strength, as a north star of sorts: "I just want to do something different that adds texture and crunch to the game. People will see things like the Ogre Loincloth, and they'll be like: 'Why does this cloth thing have strength on it?'

items.title: AMD's next-gen Zen 6 desktop CPUs are rumoured to be delayed, may be pushed back to second half of 2027
items.summary:
We got our first technical deep dive into AMD's next-generation Zen 6 CPU architecture last week, in the form of the company's new Venice range of server chips. Now there's a rumour that the consumer Ryzen chip launch may have been pushed back to the second half of 2027.

The new Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao says otherwise. In a post spotted by Videocardz , Zhang Zhonghao claims that the desktop chips, codenamed Olympic Ridge, have been switched to TSMC's N2X manufacturing process, and as a result the "timeline has been pushed back" (via machine translation).

Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year. 

Olympic Ridge was originally though to be using TSMC's N2 or N2P process node, but a switch to the performance-focussed N2X would line up with previous rumours that the chips are targeting very high clockspeeds, potentially all the way up to 6.5 GHz .

N2X is scheduled to enter production in 2027, which would explain the longer timeframe if this rumour proves out. A delay to the second half of next year would mean that Intel's Nova Lake chips, said by the company to be " tracking ahead of schedule " in a recent earnings call, would potentially have the first half of 2026 all to themselves if they launch before Zen 6.

items.title: PC gamers notice Nvidia's drivers hammering their SSDs with tens of GB/hr of unnecessary writes – revert to 621.01 ASAP
items.summary:
Another day, another dodgy driver: Nvidia's latest driver package (621.24) is needlessly writing to users' SSDs, in some cases by 30 GB every hour. And if that sounds familiar, it's because an issue with Radeon Adrenalin drivers did a similar thing a week ago.

The issue appears to be fairly widespread going from reports on the Nvidia GeForce forum , Dell forum , Super User forum , and many, many threads on Reddit . Though that's a bunch of people that might, and did, notice random writes to their SSD; many more may not visit their task manager to check these things with any regularity.

To check your own PC: 

Open Task Manager Open Details tab Right click on column header Click Select columns Find and select I/O write bytes Look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe' You can then see how much each process has written, which shouldn't usually be very much at all. I measured my own PC on an older driver version ( 621.01 ) and this process had only written 63 MB in an hour of uptime; if you're on the most recent GeForce driver package (621.24), and NVDisplay.Container.exe has a number of gigabytes next to it (it's in bytes, so get your calculator out), you've been bit by the bug. 

The affected driver, 621.24 , is still available to download right now. That's the surprising thing here, as the issue has seemingly been reported across the internet since November 15; the driver was released on November 12, and it appears to have taken a few days of needlessly huge writes for anyone to notice.

The first two episodes act as the setup for the main quest of Season 3. The premiere largely succeeds in its effort to kick off the story, and by the end of Episode 2 I found myself genuinely excited for more.

Walker Scobell has been a delightful Percy Jackson since Season 1 , but he's only gotten better with experience. items.title: GTA 6 Players Find Red Dead Redemption Lore That Strongly Suggests Both Series Are Set in the Same Universe
items.summary:
Players have found lore in GTA 6 that strongly suggest the game takes place in the same universe as Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption series, in a move that has excited fans about the prospect of a canon merger of timelines.

Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2 follow. 

We’ve already found Arthur Morgan’s hat in GTA 6, but there’s another thing connecting the two games. A readable book found in Brian’s Marina in Key Lento has multiple references to Red Dead Redemption and its sequel. X / Twitter user GameRoll shared excerpts from the book online. The book is a chronicle of the life and death of Flaco Hernandez, a gunslinger Arthur Morgan hunts to his cabin by Cairn Lake in Grizzlies West during the The Noblest of Men, and a Woman stranger mission in RDR 2. The book itself could even be the chronicle you help Theodore Levin write by hunting down the gunslingers, or at least a modern reinterpretation of it.

It’s told from the viewpoint of Rust McCreary, an original character who doesn’t appear in either RDR game. In the book, he comes across the corpse of Hernandez in the snow at Cairn Lake, right where you leave him in the RDR 2 mission. 

According to the book, Hernandez had a bullet hole right in the center of his forehead, so it’s canon that you can actually aim good. The book also references multiple locations, from New Austin to Armadillo and Blackwater. 

It’s not quite confirmation that Jason is a direct descendant of Arthur Morgan or anything like that, but it’s a cool detail that basically turns RDR into a prequel to GTA 4 and its sequels. Like…

items.title: Cyberleek Returns for GTA 6 Launch to Reportedly Release a Near-Complete Xbox Build, Threatens to Release the Game's Executable in Days

It was thought that the person or group responsible for the online Cyberleek persona had ended their spate of GTA 6 leaks last month, after their memecoin crashed despite efforts to boost its market cap.

In October, Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, and threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap. Gameplay clips reportedly leaked at the time allegedly showed Lucia fully naked — something that is not possible in the final launch version of the game.

Yesterday, November 19 — the GTA 6 release date — Cyberleek returned to drop a GTA 6 Xbox build without the game's executable. In a statement reportedly published online , Cyberleek claimed this Xbox build is a “full November 2026 build of GTA 6.” They predicted this Xbox build would be used to emulate GTA 6 on PC “within a week, running far past 30fps.”

The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

items.title: Yellowjackets Season 4, Episode 1 Review

Spoilers follow for Yellowjackets Season 4, Episode 1 – “Hivemind,” which is streaming now on Paramount+. New episodes drop weekly on Fridays. 

In 2012, Showtime delivered Yellowjackets , its best original horror drama since Dexter . Featuring a female-led cast of middle-aged legends (Melanie Lynskey, Tawny Cypress, Christina Ricci, etc.) and mostly unknowns playing their younger selves, Yellowjackets earned instant buzz for its scary mix of survival horror, social hierarchy commentary and trauma manifestations. So it’s been hugely disappointing that the subsequent two seasons have only offered diminishing returns as creators Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson (Narcos) haven’t been able to extend the potency of their original premise into coherent and compelling past and present narratives walking into Season 4.

As this is the final season, there was plenty of hope that the writing team would pour all of their reserved ideas into purposeful and emotionally rewarding narratives ignited by the plane crash survivors getting rescued from their feral, cannibalistic ways in the Canadian wilderness. Let’s be real: their return to society has long been past due as they’ve killed or eaten two-thirds of the cast. The fourth season premiere episode, “Hivemind,” crackles with the excitement of that anticipated reentry, told through 1998-era TV breaking news announcements, including Gen Z stalwart MTV News. items.title: GTA 6 is playable in first-person, here's how to activate it
items.summary:
While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park.

It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6.

As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update.

If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. If you save in first-person then immediately load the same save you'll be back in third-person and have to return to God's own preferred viewpoint.

items.title: Help: I can't stop obeying traffic laws in GTA 6
items.summary:
A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving. I'd been cruising down the Leonida Keys, and as I was patiently waiting at a red light and humming along with the radio, I had a sudden realization: I was patiently waiting at a red light. 

I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff.

There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse. 

That is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's important to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.summary:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.
items.t: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling

items.title: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying
items.summary:
I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones: boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.
items.t: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.
items.t: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
